mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLS 450 M256 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M256 inline-six is generally robust and reliable, but it has known weak points. 48V electrical system faults, coolant pump failures, timing chain noise, and oil consumption are the main concerns [8†L28-L36]. 48V battery module and electric coolant pump failures have been reported. A recall was issued for coolant pump wiring harness chafing [3†L4-L9]. Timing chain rattle on cold start can indicate tensioner wear [8†L32-L33]. Oil consumption can increase past 60,000 miles [8†L30-L31]. Carbon cleaning (walnut blasting) is recommended every ~60,000 miles [8†L33-L34].

mainEntity.name: Is the Mercedes CLS 500 M278 V8 engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M278 twin-turbo V8 is less reliable than the M256. Timing chain tensioner failure and cylinder wall scoring are the main concerns [7†L22-L25][1†L6-L7]. Timing chain rattle on cold start is common - don't ignore it [7†L22-L25]. Cylinder wall scoring can cause high oil consumption and eventual engine failure [1†L6-L7]. Have cylinders bore scoped if oil consumption is excessive [1†L10-L11]. Oil leaks from cam sensor covers and cooler seals are common. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What is the M278 cylinder scoring problem on the Mercedes CLS 500?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cylinder wall scoring (bore scoring) is a serious issue affecting the M278 V8 engine. The Alusil cylinder coating can wear, causing deep scores in the cylinder walls [1†L6-L7]. Symptoms: high oil consumption, piston slap on startup, loss of compression [1†L9-L11]. If suspected, have the cylinders bore scoped [1†L10-L11]. Repairs can cost £4,500-£6,500+, often requiring engine-out work [13†L35-L37]. A rebuilt engine with upgraded cylinder work is the only reliable fix if scoring is severe.

mainEntity.name: What is the M256 48V EQ Boost problem on the Mercedes CLS 450?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 48V electrical system that powers the EQ Boost integrated starter-alternator can suffer from battery module degradation, software corruption, or wiring issues [8†L31-L32]. Symptoms: erratic cooling, warning lights, loss of EQ Boost functionality. A recall was issued for electric coolant pump wiring harness chafing [3†L4-L9]. Specialist 48V battery module replacement costs £1,000-£1,600. Most issues stop at the 48V system - full engine replacement is rare.

mainEntity.name: How long do Mercedes CLS 450/500 modern engines last?

acceptedAnswer.text: Well-maintained M256 engines can exceed 150,000-200,000 miles. M278 V8s can also reach high mileage, but timing chain and cylinder scoring issues can occur earlier [8†L22-L23]. M256: 150k-200k+ miles with regular servicing. M256 timing chain inspection recommended from ~100,000 miles [8†L42-L43]. M278: 100k-150k+ miles if timing chain and cylinder scoring are addressed. Regular oil changes every 10,000 miles are critical for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the CLS 450 and CLS 500 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The CLS 450 uses the M256 3.0-litre inline-six with 48V EQ Boost (362-367 hp + 21 hp electric), while the CLS 500 uses the M278 4.7-litre twin-turbo V8 (408-449 hp). The CLS 500 offers more power but is less reliable and has higher running costs. CLS 450 (M256): 362-367 hp, inline-6, 48V mild hybrid, more economical. CLS 500 (M278): 408-449 hp, V8, twin-turbo, more power but higher running costs. The CLS 450 is the modern replacement for the CLS 500 in the C257 generation. The CLS 500 was produced in the C218 generation (2011-2018).

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes CLS 450/500 Modern - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes CLS 450 and CLS 500 represent the pinnacle of petrol engineering in the CLS range. The CLS 450 arrived with the third-generation C257 CLS in 2018, featuring the M256 3.0-litre inline-six with 48V EQ Boost mild-hybrid technology - Mercedes' return to the straight-six layout. The CLS 500 continued with the M278 4.7-litre twin-turbo V8, delivering effortless V8 performance until it was phased out in favour of the CLS 450 and CLS 53 AMG.

milestones.description: C218 CLS 500 launched with M278 DEH46 LA 4.7L twin-turbo V8, 408 hp, 600 Nm, 7G-TRONIC
C218 facelift: 9G-TRONIC introduced; CLS 500 power increased to 449 hp in some markets
C257 CLS 450 launched with M256 E30 DEH LA 3.0L inline-six, 362 hp + 21 hp EQ Boost, 500 Nm, 9G-TRONIC
CLS 500 discontinued in the UK; replaced by CLS 450 and CLS 53 AMG
2023 - C257 CLS produced with M256 engine across CLS 450 and CLS 53 AMG variants
C257 facelift: CLS 450 continues with M256.930, 367 hp

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes CLS 450/500 Modern Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes CLS 450 and CLS 500 are powered by two of Mercedes' most advanced petrol engines - the M256 inline-six with 48V EQ Boost and the M278 twin-turbo V8. The M256 is generally robust but suffers from 48V electrical system issues, timing chain noise, and oil consumption. The M278 twin-turbo V8 is more problematic, with well-documented timing chain tensioner failure and cylinder wall scoring that can write off engines. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty.

problems.group: M256 48V Electrical System & Coolant Pump Failure
problems.h4: M256 48V Electrical System & Coolant Pump Failure - The Modern CLS 450 Weakness
problems.rootCause: The 48V electrical system that powers the EQ Boost integrated starter-alternator and electric auxiliary compressor can suffer from battery module degradation, software corruption, or water ingress in the 48V connector. A recall was issued for the electric coolant pump - the wiring harness can chafe against the engine fan, causing malfunction or deactivation. Symptoms include erratic cooling, warning lights, and loss of EQ Boost functionality.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Dealer-level software recalibration of 48V control modules; inspect wiring harness
repairOptions.longevity: May resolve intermittent faults; only suitable for warning lights without driveability issues

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace 48V lithium-ion battery module and recalibrate system
repairOptions.longevity: Restores EQ Boost and electric compressor function

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace electric coolant pump and repair wiring harness
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; recall covers some models

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M256 with updated 48V components and full software configuration
repairOptions.longevity: Only required if internal engine damage has occurred from hybrid system faults; rare

problems.recommendation: M256 electrical faults are frustrating but rarely write off the engine itself. Start with a specialist diagnostic and software update before replacing hardware. Full engine replacement is exceptionally rare on this engine family - most issues stop at the 48V battery, coolant pump, or software level. Use a Mercedes-Benz specialist with M256 hybrid experience, not a general independent.

problems.group: M256 Timing Chain Noise & Oil Consumption
problems.h4: M256 Timing Chain Noise & Oil Consumption - Maintenance Concerns
problems.rootCause: The M256 timing chain tensioners rely on oil pressure to maintain chain tension. When the engine is stood for a period, oil can drain from the tensioners, causing a brief rattling noise on cold start. This is often harmless if brief, but persistent rattle indicates wear. Oil consumption can increase past 60,000 miles due to carbon buildup or PCV system issues. Carbon buildup on intake valves due to direct injection is also a concern.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; brief cold start rattle only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioners, guides and sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Required if persistent rattle or chain stretch is confirmed

Comprehensive oil consumption test, bore scope inspection, PCV system check
repairOptions.longevity: Required to determine root cause of oil consumption

repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or oil consumption is due to piston ring wear

problems.recommendation: A brief rattle on cold start (1-2 seconds) is often normal, but persistent rattle requires attention. Carbon cleaning is recommended every 60,000 miles on M256 engines. If you're topping up oil frequently, get a consumption test - the digital oil level readout can be unreliable.

problems.h4: M278 Timing Chain Tensioner Failure - Rattling Noise on Cold Start
problems.rootCause: The M278 timing chain tensioners can fail, causing a "bag of nails" rattle on cold start. Timing chain tensioner failures have been reported in M278 V8 engines, contributing to rattling noises and oil contamination of engine wiring. If ignored, the chain can jump and cause catastrophic valve/piston contact.

repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; cold start rattle only

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioners, guides and sprockets. Engine-out job
repairOptions.longevity: Required if persistent rattle or chain stretch is confirmed

problems.recommendation: Rattling on cold start is the early warning sign. Don't ignore it - specialist timing chain replacement at £2,500-£3,800 resolves the issue if done promptly. If the chain has already slipped, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the only safe option.

problems.h4: M278 Cylinder Wall Scoring - The Most Serious M278 Failure
problems.rootCause: Cylinder wall scoring (bore scoring) is the most serious problem affecting the M278 engine. The Alusil cylinder coating can wear, causing deep scores in the cylinder walls. Symptoms include high oil consumption, piston slap on startup, and eventual loss of compression. If suspected, have the cylinders bore scoped. Repairs can cost $10,000+, with sleeving being a major engine-out job.

repairOptions.longevity: Required if scoring is severe or bottom-end damage has occurred

problems.recommendation: Cylinder wall scoring is the single most serious issue affecting the M278 engine. If your CLS 500 is consuming oil, have the cylinders bore scoped immediately. If scoring is detected, a rebuilt engine with upgraded cylinder work is the only reliable fix. On a car worth less than £10,000, replacement may not be cost-effective - consider your options carefully.
